title: Synthetic Probe Reconciler: Non-Destructive Runbook + Terraform Repair Runner for Private VPC Health Failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) customer nodes intermittently fail health checks (service probes, control-plane heartbeats, egress DNS resolution). Existing alarms are noisy and current remediation runbooks either require manual approval or perform heavy-handed terraform replacements that cause transient capacity loss.

Goal: Implement a Synthetic Probe Reconciler runbook and an accompanying lightweight Terraform Repair Runner that: (1) automatically triages common, non-destructive failures detected by health probes, (2) attempts reversible fixes in a safe order (config reconciliation, network policy refresh, DNS cache flush, kubelet restart), and (3) only escalates to destructive actions (node replace, terraform taint/apply) after gating and operator approval. The implementation should be observable, auditable, and reversible; include small, testable automation pieces and clear operator prompts.

Scope: design and implement the runbook, wire Telemetry -> Reconciler alerting, author a Terraform Repair Runner module for limited automated remediation (not full auto-replace), create automated test harness and canary rollout plan, add console runbook links and a post-action audit trail in S3/console.

Out of scope: fully automated node replacements (unsupervised), major changes to terraform modules beyond safe guardrails, private-control-plane architectural changes.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic Probe Reconciler triggers on two or more correlated probe failures across the same node within a rolling 2-minute window
Reconciler performs a defined non-destructive sequence: config reconcile -> network-policy refresh -> DNS cache flush -> kubelet restart; success stops further remediation

Terraform Repair Runner exposes explicit, idempotent steps for state-only repairs (reapply modules with changed metadata, refresh remote state, reconcile tags) and requires operator confirmation for taint/apply operations
All automated actions are logged with unique run IDs, runbook links, and a human-readable justification in S3 (or customer audit store) and visible in Console runbook panel
Automated unit/integration tests cover simulated probe failure -> reconciler run -> success and probe failure -> gated rollback flows
Canary rollout to 10% of private clusters with kill-switch and immediate rollback path validated
Runbook includes clear escalation paths, SLAs for human-in-the-loop actions, and post-mortem templates
runbook_steps: 1) Alarm fires: Correlated synthetic probe failures detected (probe IDs: probe-ctrlplane-tcp, probe-redis-tcp, probe-kv-heartbeat)
2) Reconciler gathers context: node metadata, recent terraform plan/apply history, kubelet logs (last 5m), network policy diffs, DNS resolution traces, security group changes

3) Non-destructive attempt sequence (automated):
  a) Reconcile node labels/annotations from IaC metadata (no restart)
  b) Refresh network policies by reapplying CALICO policy manifest with dry-run + apply if no diff
  c) Trigger DNS cache flush on node agent via a small SSH-less agent RPC (controlled RPC cred only)
  d) Restart kubelet service (graceful stop/start with health probe backoff)
  e) Wait 30s and re-run probes; if green, mark incident resolved
4) If non-destructive steps fail: escalate to operator with pre-populated remediation checklist and 'one-click' terraform repair dry-run results

5) Operator confirmation: upon approval, Terraform Repair Runner executes limited state operations (terraform refresh, reconcile tags, force-recreate specific resource if flagged) with explicit taint/apply only after a second confirmation
6) Post-action: collect logs, associated PR/TF plan links, attach run ID to incident, and schedule a follow-up post-mortem if customer impact is high
automation_spec: Reconciler service: small stateless lambda-style service (k8s Job or Fargate) that subscribes to probe-topic (Kafka/CloudPubSub) and makes decisions via rule engine (Drools-style or simple priority queue)
Decision rules stored as YAML in repo with feature flags (fflags) to enable/disable specific remediation steps per-customer
Repair Runner SDK: terraform wrapper (Go) that supports dry-run, plan snapshots, human approval tokens, and run-id tagging in state bucket
RBAC: actions require signed operator token; automated 'low-risk' steps allowed under service principal with limited IAM scope; all actions recorded to audit log with immutable run IDs
Circuit breakers: per-cluster rate limits, global kill-switch, and exponential backoff on repeated failures (3 attempts max for automated steps)
rollback_criteria: If probes do not recover within 3 minutes after a kubelet restart -> abort further automation and mark as Escalated
If terraform plan indicates destructive changes affecting >1 resource in a single resource group -> cancel automated apply and require manual review
If any automated action increases 5xx errors in control-plane metrics by >10% in a 5m window -> immediate rollback of the step (if reversible) and operator alert
Operator can trigger manual rollback via Console runbook UI which will execute reverse steps captured in the run snapshot
test_plan: Unit tests for decision rules (simulate probe payloads and assert chosen actions)
Integration test: local cluster test harness that injects DNS failures, network policy drops, and kubelet hang to validate non-destructive remediation sequence
Chaos test: run reconciler against canary clusters under controlled chaos experiments (kubelet OOM, iptables flush) and verify safety gates
E2E: Canary rollout automation verifying 10% cluster coverage, observability dashboards, and operator acceptance tests
Security: run IaC scanner on Terraform Repair Runner and ensure least-privilege IAM policies; include a red-team attempt to misuse operator token
